i-finally-graduated-and-whats-next-for-t.title: I finally graduated, and what's next for this channel
i-finally-graduated-and-whats-next-for-t.excerpt: A thank you, a short look back, and what to expect next from the channel and this website, now that I have finally graduated.
i-finally-graduated-and-whats-next-for-t.content:
I finally graduated. I have been typing that sentence in my head for a long time, and it still feels a little unreal to see it written down. So this post is a thank you, a small look back, and a promise about what this channel and website are going to be from here.

What graduating means to me

I studied the Diploma in Perioperative Theatre Technology at Reliance Africa School of Health Sciences in Kitale. Along the way I learned that good theatre work is made of small, careful habits: the checks before the patient arrives, the counts, the sterile technique, the pauses on the safety checklist. Nothing flashy. Just people doing the boring parts properly, every time.

Graduating does not mean I know everything. It means I have a solid foundation, and now I get to keep learning in the open and share it with you.

Thank you

Thank you to my family, my lecturers, my classmates and everyone who read a post, watched a video, shared a card or sent a kind message. You made it easier to keep going on days when I did not feel like it.

What happens next on this channel

  • More episodes of Perioperative Theatre Technology. The first ten episodes cover the overview, sterilisation, tables and diathermy, anaesthesia machines, instruments and sutures, infection prevention, positioning, counts and records, laparoscopic equipment and emergencies. More will follow.
  • More content cards and study material on this website, written in plain language so revision is quicker.
  • More real talk. Storytime videos about the journey: the lessons, the mistakes and the things I wish someone had told me.
  • Your questions. Tell me what you want explained next, and I will do my best to cover it.

A small request

Everything here is free to read and watch, and I want to keep it that way. If the site has helped you, you can support it with a small M-Pesa donation. If you read a lot of posts, you may see a gentle reminder to do that. It helps with hosting and with making new episodes and study cards.

Now tell me: what would you like to see next? Leave a comment under the video, or message me through the contact page. The link to read more is always in the description.

Stay humble, stay safe, and thank you for being here.
